headline: Pretrained sequence models are probed against DMS, structure and splicing tasks,…
label: Biological Sequence Foundation Models
summary: New preprints extend DNA, RNA and protein models to variant, glycosylation and cancer tasks while benchmarks expose ligand invariance and reading-frame…
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretrained or self-supervised sequence representations applied to downstream biological prediction, though items differ in modality. IsoAlign aligns DNA with protein isoforms via JEPA, LIMBER combines self-attention and Mamba on 40.5M ncRNA sequences, and MMRL learns somatic missense representations from ~50,000 tumors that outperform TMB for prognosis. MaskNGly uses protein language model embeddings zero-shot for N-glycosylation, and ESMRank fuses ranks across ~1100 deep mutational scans, outperforming baselines on ProteinGym. Newer is the emphasis on diagnosing what models learn: MET kinase scans across 11 inhibitors show largely ligand-invariant predictions, and black-box splice predictors depend on reading-frame information unavailable to the splicing machinery.
